STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a flat white square plate with a rim band and flat centre, no inner wall. Flat plate, square.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks like a standard large dinner plate, so about 26 cm.
b) Reference: broccoli florets are about 4 cm. The plate spans roughly 6-7 florets across its width (about 380-400 px in a ~480 px-tall frame, with florets around 60-70 px). Using 6.5 florets x 4 cm = 26 cm. Both cues agree.
Final width: 26 cm square, area = 26^2 = 676 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Rice (white, cooked): mound roughly 8 cm x 6 cm footprint, covering about 9% of the plate area is too high; estimate footprint ~50 cm². Thickness: a grain clump is about 0.5 cm, stacked ~4 deep at the peak, so average about 1.5-2 cm. Volume ≈ 50 x 1.7 ≈ 85 ml. Grams ≈ 85 x 0.8 ≈ 70 g. Rice is only visible on one side, so I'll take ~80 g.
- Steak (sliced beef, medium-rare, two pieces): footprint of the central piece ~45 cm² plus the right-side strips ~50 cm², total ~95 cm². Average thickness ~1 cm (the pieces are thin, about 0.8-1 cm). Volume ≈ 95 ml; grams ≈ 95 x 1.0 ≈ 95 g.
- Broccoli (about 5-6 florets, cooked): footprint ~70 cm², thickness of a floret cluster ~2 cm at peak, averaging ~1 cm. Volume ≈ 70 ml; chopped vegetables at 0.6 g/ml gives ~45 g. Florets look like a little more mass, so ~50 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No clear base layer under the rice or steak beyond what is shown. No additional items added.

STEP 5 - Energy per 100 g (cooked):
- Cooked white rice: about 130 kcal/100 g.
- Cooked beef steak (medium-rare, lean-to-fatty cut): about 220 kcal/100 g.
- Cooked broccoli: about 35 kcal/100 g.

Totals: rice 80 g ≈ 104 kcal; beef 95 g ≈ 209 kcal; broccoli 50 g ≈ 18 kcal. Total ≈ 330 kcal, about 225 g.
